clue.text: Move slowly in church

parts.note: taken as written; that the clue words in church also begin with the same run of letters is a coincidence of the charade

explanation.surface: Someone creeping quietly down the aisle during a service.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward a little at a time is a gradual, creeping kind of progress.

clue.text: Fail to sustain staff? About right

indicators.note: the word for staff goes round, or about, the letter for right

parts.note: a stave is a stout stick or staff

explanation.surface: Asking whether underpaying employees is a failure to support them, and whether that is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as employees, but it is a wooden stick, a STAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive of food is to withhold the nourishment that keeps a body going.

clue.text: An environment that's virtually defined?

parts.note: virtually seems to mean almost, but it points to virtual reality: a world existing only online, inside computer networks

explanation.surface: A place described as all but defined, nearly given a clear identity.
explanation.definitionFit: The online realm of computer networks is a virtual environment rather than a physical place.

clue.text: Tense son in a competition misbehaves

indicators.note: the letters for tense and son sit inside the word for a competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition, as in the FA Cup
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A nervous boy behaving badly at a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the son; it is the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: To play up is to behave badly, as an unruly child or faulty machine does.

clue.text: Colossal run some misjudged? Nothing in it

indicators.note: nothing, as a letter, goes in the rearranged letters (it refers back to them)
the words run and some are judged wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A cricketer or athlete misjudging some runs so badly that the outcome is huge, or trivially small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misjudged' makes ENRMOUS, the anagram, and 'in' sets the O inside it. 'Nothing in it' reads as a shrug at the size, but it is the letter O for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of vast, gigantic size.

clue.text: Advantage gained from advertising free of government

indicators.note: the word for advertising is set free of the letter for government, which is dropped

parts.note: plugs are bits of publicity promoting something

explanation.surface: A benefit that comes from advertising once official interference is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUGS loses G, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a positive point or benefit, the opposite of a minus.

clue.text: A flighty sort in duet played air

indicators.note: the bird sits inside the rearranged letters
the duet is played, so the letters of duet are rearranged

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a creature of flight

explanation.surface: A frivolous singer joining a duet and performing a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' makes TUDE, and 'in' puts the bird inside. 'air' looks like a tune to go with the duet; it is the definition, meaning a manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or bearing, as in putting on airs, the outward stance someone adopts.

clue.text: Singular post of a romantic sort?

definitions.text: Singular post of a romantic sort?

parts.words: Singular post of a romantic sort?
parts.note: singular post suggests something odd, but it is just one piece of mail, sent by an admirer

explanation.surface: A peculiar job or position with a romantic flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is a single piece of mail declaring affection to a sweetheart.

clue.text: Smart man at typewriter retained

indicators.note: the letters are kept within the run of words man at typewriter

explanation.surface: A well-dressed fellow kept on at the typewriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and stylishly dressed, as dapper does.

clue.text: Some poetry including representation of late artist

indicators.note: the word for some poetry takes in the reworked letters

parts.note: a canto is one section of a long poem

indicators.note: a representation of the word late renders its letters in a new form

explanation.surface: A section of verse that includes a portrait of a dead painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation of' makes ALET, which 'including' sets inside the poetry. 'late' looks like it means dead; here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter famous for views of Venice.

clue.text: Control part of parachute?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the steering of a parachute is one of its components.
explanation.definitionFit: To harness is to bring under control and use; the harness is the set of straps attaching a parachutist to the canopy.

clue.text: Delay concerning impish chap right away

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: right goes away, so its letter is dropped from the word for the impish chap

parts.note: a sprite is a mischievous elf or fairy

explanation.surface: A hold-up caused by a mischievous figure running off at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like a phrase meaning immediately; 'away' drops R from SPRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a pause or reprieve, a postponement of something unwelcome.

clue.text: Game in boxes time forgot

indicators.note: the word for boxes forgets, so loses, the letter for time

parts.note: chests are large storage boxes

explanation.surface: A board game kept in boxes long forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game of strategy for two players.

clue.text: Misshapen hat we fetch producing gossip

indicators.note: the words hat we fetch are put out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fetching a battered hat and chatting idly about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat at length in an idle, informal way is an idiom for gossiping.

clue.text: Method dour creep deployed

indicators.note: the words dour creep are deployed, set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sullen, sneaky person putting a plan into action.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is an established way of doing something, a set routine.

clue.text: City with varied menu I term largely of broad appeal

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: the words menu I are varied, so their letters are rearranged
largely means most of the word for term, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to call something is to term or name it

explanation.surface: A city restaurant with a diverse menu, said to be of wide appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' turns MENU I into UMENI; 'largely' cuts CALL to CAL. 'City' is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical means universal or inclusive, embracing many groups, especially Christian churches.

clue.text: Fresher abroad?

parts.note: a fresher is a first-year undergraduate in Britain; this one is studying in another country under a swap scheme

explanation.surface: Something fresher in a foreign land, like air or produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresher' is the British word for a new university student.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil spending time at a foreign school or university under a reciprocal scheme.

clue.text: Vehicle left with northerly people? Suspended vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading the word for people upwards

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A taxi leaving with travellers from the north, then a hanging carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northerly' turns RACE into ECAR, since in a down answer north is upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car is a cabin hanging from an overhead wire, carrying passengers up mountains.

clue.text: Conservationists probing man in English town

indicators.note: the conservationists probe, so go inside, the man's name

parts.note: Graham is a man's name
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: Environmentalists questioning a man in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: GRANTHAM is a market town in Lincolnshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Grantham is a market town in Lincolnshire, birthplace of Margaret Thatcher.

clue.text: Dishes, perhaps, with a beer Walt cooked

indicators.note: the words a beer Walt are cooked, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Walt preparing a meal using beer, served in dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, bowls and cutlery are all items for the dining table; dishes are an example.

clue.text: Treat a stiff type?

parts.note: treating a stiff sounds like dealing with a rigid person, but a stiff is slang for a corpse to be preserved

explanation.surface: Dealing with a formal, rigid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalmers preserve a dead body with chemicals to delay decay.

clue.text: Sharp English drink left out

indicators.note: left is taken out, so its letter goes from the word for the drink

parts.note: lager is a light beer

explanation.surface: A keen Englishman whose drink has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: LAGER loses L to become AGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp and keen both describe strong enthusiasm.

clue.text: Cheap booze obtained around university? Teacher's gutted

indicators.note: the word for obtained goes round the other pieces

parts.note: got means obtained

indicators.note: the word for teacher is gutted, its inside letters removed

parts.note: a tutor is a teacher; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A teacher devastated after getting cheap drink around campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like upset; it empties the teacher, leaving TR, and 'around' wraps the word for obtained about U and TR. Rotgut is slang the solver may know in the reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotgut is a slang term for cheap, poor-quality alcohol that upsets the stomach.

clue.text: Girl before break obtaining highest point?

indicators.note: the girl comes before the word for break

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A young woman taking a break before the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's tallest mountain, its summit the loftiest peak.

clue.text: Novel girl?

explanation.surface: Asking whether an unusual young woman is new.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen, and also a common female name.

clue.text: Fragile UK citizen let off

parts.note: a Brit is a British person

indicators.note: off suggests the word let is spoiled or disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British citizen released from custody, emotionally delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittle means easily broken, as fragile things are.

clue.text: Test warnings? Not half!

indicators.note: only half of the word for warnings is wanted, its first four letters

parts.note: an example made of someone serves as a warning to others

explanation.surface: Checking warnings, emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for very much so; here it keeps half of EXAMPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: A prank almost by host before everyone — it has a rousing effect!

indicators.note: the host comes before the word for everyone
almost means the word for prank loses its last letter

parts.note: a lark is a piece of fun or a prank
MC is a master of ceremonies, a host
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A practical joke by a party host in front of the crowd that wakes everyone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake-up call rouses a sleeper at an arranged time.

clue.text: Odour created by a Catholic mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the word for Catholic loses its last letter

parts.note: Roman is used for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A smell given off by a Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell, usually a pleasant one.
